sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 20.03.2024.

The following arguments made by Sri Divanshu Tiwari, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Sri Akhilendra Yadav, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Suchit Tandon, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 16 years in the prosecution case only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant contests the age of the victim set out in the prosecution case in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P.
and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) is contested on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.

entities.text:
Monish Vs. State of U.P.
and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no lawful basis for the age related entry in the school record.
The school records disclosing her age as 16 years 4 months are unreliable.

(iii) No medical examination to determine the correct age of the victim as per the latest scientific criteria and medical protocol by eminent doctors from a reputed institution was got done by the prosecution as the same would have established the majority of the victim and falsified the prosecution case.
The victim is in fact a major.
3. The delay in lodgment of the FIR is fatal to the prosecution case in the facts and circumstances of this case.
4. The applicant and the victim were intimate.
5. The FIR was lodged after their relationship was exposed when the victim was found in a compromising position with the applicant at the house of the applicant by the mother of the victim.
6. The victim in her statement under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and Section 164 Cr.P.C. has admitted that she was in regular contact with the applicant and went to his house of her own free will.

7. False and aggravated allegations were made by the victim in her statement under Section 164 CrPC at the behest of her family members only to deflect attention from her own conduct and to save the failing prosecution case.
Even if the statement under Section 164 CrPC is taken on its face value no specific allegation of rape has been made against the applicant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Major inconsistencies in the F.I.R., statements of the victim under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and under Section 164 Cr.P.C. discredit the prosecution case.
9. Medical evidence to establish commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
10. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
11. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Manish Kumar Jha be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii )
The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

(iii) The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru.
Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. (Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
